name: Texas Metal Works
old_description: Professional-grade welding tables, modular booths, and precision tooling engineered for shops that demand more. Every product is designed, cut, and welded at our facility in Texas.
about:
Texas Metal Works operates from a 40,000-square-foot, climate-controlled facility in Conroe, Texas. The company was founded in 2017 by brothers John and Kirk Pozadzides, who started the business after failing to find quality, affordable American-made fabrication tables for their own shop. They built the first tables for themselves, then brought them to market.

The company manufactures professional-grade welding tables, modular welding booths, heavy-duty workbenches, plasma cutting tables, DIY welding kits, and the ModPro modular storage system. Production runs on precision laser cutters, CNC press brakes, and robotic welding cells, with in-house powder coating available in over 200 colors. Texas Metal Works offers more than 40 standard table variants in sizes from 30″×30″ to 70″×140″, all cut from ASTM A572-50 structural steel milled in the U.S. It also produces the only readily available stainless-steel fabrication table line in the domestic market.

Customers range from hobbyist garages and small fabrication shops to large production facilities, as well as school districts, community colleges, and CTE programs nationwide. The stainless tables serve contamination-sensitive sectors such as food-grade, pharmaceutical, aerospace, and high-purity welding. Structural steel fabrication services support commercial, industrial, and institutional projects.

Texas Metal Works emphasizes its ISO 9001 certified quality system, AWS-certified welders, and a 100% debt-free, brother-owned structure that answers only to customers. Manufacturing, fabrication, shipping, and U.S.-based support all operate under one roof, allowing control over tolerances, flatness, and lead times without third-party handoffs.

name: Texas Sheet Metal Services
old_description: We have custom fabrication experience with a variety of metals, including stainless steel, carbon steel, aluminum, and a number of exotic alloys.
about:
Texas Sheet Metal Services operates from Needville, Texas, a privately owned precision fabrication shop founded in 2013. In 2021 the company acquired the assets of Fojtik Sheet Metal Works, a business started in 1989 by Thomas Fojtik, and partnered with Cisco’s Sheet Metal for roof installation, bringing together decades of sheet metal heritage.

The shop provides custom sheet metal fabrication including welding, laser cutting, equipment repair, brush finishing, and powder coating, along with full-service metal roofing installation, repair, storm-damage restoration, and elastomeric coating. With a team of about 30, they produce components such as standing-seam roof panels, flashing, wall panels, and soffit panels for both residential and commercial projects.

Customers span residential homeowners, commercial builders, agricultural operators, oil-and-gas facilities, HVAC contractors, schools, churches, and historical-restoration projects. Past work includes a stainless-steel kitchen island top, a repaired feeder, a cotton-picker mailbox, and refurbished church steeples, demonstrating the shop’s ability to handle one-off custom pieces as well as larger building envelopes.

The company emphasizes accurate estimates, realistic timelines, and a safety-first approach with no shortcuts. Its stated goal is to fabricate custom equipment that meets evolving customer needs while maintaining competitive pricing, leveraging the combined experience of the Fojtik and Cisco’s Sheet Metal legacies.

name: Textile USA, Inc.
old_description: Since 1995 an embroidery supplies wholesaler | Quality & excellent service [Eng/Esp] 🟡 Do More with Less 🟡
about:
Textile USA, Inc. was founded in Miami, Florida in March 2003, building on embroidery industry experience dating back to 1995. The company operates as a wholesale distributor of embroidery thread and supplies, positioning itself as a primary source for embroidery professionals across the southeastern United States. Ownership structure and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company stocks a broad inventory of embroidery consumables including rayon, polyester, and metallic threads from brands such as Marathon, Tristar, and Viscose; cutaway and tear-away backings in various weights; 3D foam and felt; Organ and Schmetz needles; Mundial, Kai, and Belmont scissors; and a range of adhesives, lubricants, and cleaning fluids. Textile USA serves as the exclusive vendor of Marathon Thread for the southeastern United States and emphasizes factory-direct pricing on its catalog of several hundred SKUs.

Customers include commercial embroidery shops, decorated-apparel producers, and entrepreneurs launching new embroidery businesses. The company's bilingual (English/Spanish) support team serves clients throughout the region, with orders fulfilled from its Miami facility.

Textile USA states that its differentiation rests on factory-direct pricing, a comprehensive on-hand inventory, and a service philosophy centered on long-term relationships, on-time delivery, and post-sale support. The Marathon brand it exclusively distributes carries Oeko-Tex Standard 100 and ISO 9001 certifications.

name: The Big Screen Store
old_description: CALL OR VISIT FOR LOWER IN-STORE ONLY PRICING. MON-SAT 11-7 SUN 12-5
about:
The Big Screen Store was founded in 1996 in Annapolis, Maryland. The company operates as a specialty retailer of Samsung televisions and soundbars, with a network of 11 showrooms across the region. The business remains privately held, though ownership structure is not publicly disclosed.

The store carries a focused lineup of Samsung models, including the S95H, R85H, and R95H series, which are offered as showroom and site exclusives not available through third-party marketplaces such as Amazon. Each location allows side-by-side comparison using live streaming content rather than canned demos, letting buyers evaluate picture quality on the shows and sports they watch at home. Services include free white-glove delivery and setup on the customer's schedule, as well as lifetime technical support accessible by phone for as long as the purchaser owns the TV.

The business serves residential and light-commercial customers seeking premium home-theater displays and audio. Its price-match policy promises to beat advertised prices from Best Buy, Amazon, and Costco — or the purchase is free — with sales tax instantly absorbed on every Samsung TV and soundbar purchase.

The company emphasizes a no-upsell service model: lifetime support carries no annual renewal or tiered fees, and the retailer positions its in-store experience as a quieter, appointment-driven alternative to big-box environments, offering booked floor time so that models of interest are ready for demonstration.

name: The Brickle Group
old_description: H. Brickle Fiber Trading & Recycling specializes in combining virgin and recycled fibers to deliver tailored solutions for your manufacturing needs.
about:
The Brickle Group is headquartered in Woonsocket, Rhode Island, where it began as a third‑generation family business founded by Hyman Brickle in 1937. After working for a local rag merchant, Hyman launched H. Brickle & Son, Inc. to trade recycled fibers between textile mills, becoming the first woolen waste dealer in the South and establishing a foundation built on material recovery.

Today the group operates six divisions. Bouckaert Industrial Textiles custom‑engineers needle‑punch nonwoven felts. Northwest Woolen Mills has produced wool and synthetic blankets for 68 years, supplying army blankets and emergency‑relief blankets for humanitarian crises worldwide. H. Brickle Fiber Trading & Recycling purchases mill waste, recycles it, and spins woolen yarns (including 2‑ to 4‑ply constructions) for other textile manufacturers. F&M Dyeing Corp provides commercial‑quality dyeing and fulling for wool and fur felt hat bodies. Brickle Realty Group manages and develops industrial and commercial properties, while Heat Smart assembles energy‑assistance kits — wool blankets, weatherstripping, and conservation tips — for low‑income households.

Customers span textile mills, hat manufacturers, government agencies (including the U.S. Department of Energy), disaster‑relief organizations, and senior‑energy programs. The group's blankets have been deployed in natural disasters and political conflicts globally, and its fiber‑recycling services feed raw material back into the textile supply chain.

The company credits its longevity to diversification — acquiring Northwest Woolen Mills in 1978 and Bouckaert Industrial Textiles in 2000 — and to a mission of developing tailored products while maintaining a culture rooted in family, quality of life, and performance.

name: The Colorado Tent Company
old_description: No ice. No insulated pack. No added weight. Just physics — and Belgian linen that has been doing this job since 1940.
about:
The Colorado Tent Company operates from Denver, Colorado, tracing its roots to 1890 when the Denver Tent and Awning Company opened on Larimer Street to serve miners, ranchers, railroad crews, and military posts. A second shop, the Colorado Tent & Awning Company, was founded by Robert S. Gutshall in 1899 on Lawrence Street. The two competitors merged in 2003, and in 2022 the business was acquired by Harlan and Karah Hummer, who retained the existing team and standards.

The company handcrafts canvas wall tents, tipis, awnings, and custom shelter goods at its facility at 10975 E. 55th Avenue. Every tent is cut, sewn, and inspected by hand using 10.10‑oz Sunforger® marine‑grade cotton duck, double‑stitched seams, and brass hardware. Production runs are limited each month, with a current lead time of three to six weeks for both stock and custom orders.

Customers span hunting outfitters, camps and non‑profits, glamping and hospitality operators, event and gathering planners, and commercial and corporate clients. Historical contracts include military, scouting, and ranching accounts.

The shop differentiates itself through a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects, a repair‑first design philosophy (no glues or seals that prevent future fixes), and adherence to the same materials and methods used since the early 1900s.

name: The Durham Company
old_description: Both beautiful and functional, natural fences are a fragrant and attractive way of creating privacy.
about:
The Durham Company has operated from Lebanon, Missouri since its founding in 1959. The privately held business is led by CEO G.T. Carr and has grown to serve the electric utility sector with a focus on metering and distribution equipment.

The company manufactures a range of electrical utility products including meter sockets, socket breaker enclosures, electrical connectors, instrument-rated transformers, test switches, pad-mount equipment, and enclosures for breakers, current transformers, and voltage transformers. It also produces pole-mount brackets and underground distribution equipment, offering custom variations to meet specific utility requirements. The firm emphasizes innovative engineering and continuous improvement across its manufacturing processes.

Primary customers are electric utilities and companies in the electrical distribution chain. The company's expansion into Buffalo, Missouri, announced in collaboration with the City of Buffalo, Dallas County R-I School District, Dallas County, and the Missouri Department of Economic Development, underscores its role as a regional employer.

The Durham Company cites its "World Class Experience" of over 60 years, innovative engineering and design, continuous improvement in all processes, and customer service as its defining differentiators.
